name: gix v0.90.0
body:
### New Features (BREAKING)

 - add worktree locking and a lock override that preserves changes
   <!-- agent -->
   Expose `Worktree::set_lock(Option<&BStr>)` and `worktree::Proxy::set_lock()`
   so callers can protect linked worktrees from pruning, moving, or removal,
   including when their checkout is offline. Implement file handling in
   `gix_worktree::set_lock()`: preserve byte-oriented reasons, append Git's
   trailing newline when needed, and make unlocking idempotent. Reject the
   main worktree in the porcelain and avoid writing through lock-file symlinks.
   
   Previously `Force::OverrideLock` also discarded local changes and initialized
   submodules. Add `Force::OverrideLockKeepChanges` to bypass just the lock check,
   retaining status and submodule validation. This expands an exhaustive public
   enum, so adapt the Tix caller in the same commit; existing CLI force levels
   retain their behavior.
   
   Git reference: `v2.56.0-116-g6de20f6092`
   (`6de20f6092dcf9bdb1c8efe03db4b70c82b423dd`), `builtin/worktree.c`
   lock/unlock/removal, `wrapper.c` newline encoding, and
   `t/t2403-worktree-move.sh`. Git's `worktree remove -ff` bypasses both lock and
   cleanliness checks; the new mode deliberately permits bypassing only the lock.
   exposes a pre-existing unresolved `with_fetch_options` link in clone docs.

### Test

 - worktree removal with late writes to both roots
   <!-- agent -->
   Inject bounded writes through removal progress after scanning, proving that
   one-pass deletion leaves files while default retries finish.

### Performance

 - don't look for new packs before writing an object

### Reverted (BREAKING)

 - remove the obsolete `max-performance-safe` feature
   <!-- agent -->
   `gix` always uses `zlib-rs`, so the safe bundle no longer differs from
   `max-performance`. Make `max-performance` own the default cache setup and
   update defaults, cache tests, and developer commands. Downstream users of
   the removed name must select `max-performance` instead.

### New Features

 - add `Submodule::resolved_url()` for cloning
   Definitely went through the tests quickly, besides the usual
   'make it a shell script', but poked the URL resolution and Windows
   special cases.
   Some of the newly added drive-prefix tests are truly from another world,
   and I don't think I could ever have written those, for better or worse.
   
   <!-- agent -->
   Relative submodule URLs in `.gitmodules` refer to the superproject's
   upstream, even when that upstream uses `ssh://`, `git://`, or SCP syntax.
   Passing the existing `Submodule::url()` result directly to a clone treats
   `./` and `../` entries as local paths instead.
   
   Document `url()` as the raw configured accessor and add `resolved_url()`
   for cloning or fetching. Port Git's byte-oriented `relative_url()` rules
   from `remote.c`, select the current branch's remote or the default remote,
   and fall back to the superproject itself when the selected URL is missing.
   Make local paths absolute so the result does not depend on the caller's
   working directory. Honor configuration overrides as initialized URLs,
   avoiding a second remote-relative resolution of local URLs written by
   `git submodule init`.
   
   Validate transport and local URLs, traversal errors, default-remote
   selection, initialized overrides, unborn and bare repositories, and
   non-UTF-8 local paths in disposable repositories. Compare resolution with
   `git submodule init`; include native-separator coverage for Windows.
 - expose selected global attribute paths
   <!-- agent -->
   Allow callers that retain detached diff results to track the attribute files
   selected by the repository. Reuse the existing resolver so permissions,
   configuration interpolation, fallback paths, and precedence stay consistent
   with the attribute stack.
   
   Return selected paths even when files are missing so their later creation can
   invalidate cached results. Per-directory attributes and `info/attributes`
   remain separate because their locations are already known to the caller.
 - provide safe interrupt setup and handle `SIGHUP`
   <!-- agent -->
   Applications that only need the shared cancellation flag should not have to
   supply an unsafe signal callback. Add `interrupt::init_handler_default()` as a
   safe entry point while preserving the callback and grace policy of an existing
   registration, including when a UI runs inside the `gix` command.
   
   Treat Unix `SIGHUP` like the other termination signals so long-running work can
   observe cancellation and callers can restore terminal state before exiting.
   It previously bypassed the shared flag and terminated immediately. Repeated
   signals retain the existing forced-termination policy.
   
   Exercise all supported termination signals and nested safe registration in
   isolated subprocesses. Four interrupt tests pass with the feature enabled and
   two pass without it.
 - add `Remote::default_branch()` to learn the default branch of a remote without connecting to it.
   `git clone` and `git remote set-head` record the default branch of a remote in the symbolic reference
   `refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD`, which points to the remote-tracking branch of that branch, like
   `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Since Git 2.48, `git fetch` also creates it if it's missing.
 - make repository paths absolute without reloading
   <!-- Byron -->
   
   Went through the tests quite quickly, thinking their are deep and thorough
   as usual.
   
   <!-- agent -->
   Relative repository paths depend on the process current directory. Changing it
   after opening a repository can redirect checkout validation, Git-link handling,
   HEAD and object reads, or index persistence away from the intended repository.
   
   Add `Repository::make_paths_absolute()` to anchor the selected Git directory,
   common directory, worktree, index, and object database to the CWD captured at
   opening. Unlike `reload()`, this keeps runtime configuration, reference namespaces,
   and in-memory objects. Join paths lexically so missing worktrees remain supported
   and destination symlinks are still rejected. Leave existing clones unchanged,
   avoid partial updates on failure, and make repeated calls a no-op.
   
   Recreate relative reference and object stores through their existing APIs.
   Reset caches carrying relative index paths or store-specific pack IDs while
   preserving outstanding snapshots.
   
   Use an anchored repository view for initial checkout, and anchor global attribute
   paths before optional-file metadata checks. Document the interpolation helper
   and its captured-directory behavior.
   
   Cover CWD changes, main and linked worktrees, bare repositories, missing checkouts,
   index overrides, retained runtime state, idempotence, and failed reconstruction.
   Include a Windows-only test for rejecting unresolved drive-relative index paths
   without partially updating the repository.
 - separate linked worktree registration from checkout
   <!-- Byron -->
   
   Skipped over the tests, knowing they are very detailed
   can be trusted by now.
   
   <!-- agent -->
   Add `Repository::prepare_add_worktree()` with consuming checkout and explicit
   persistence. Persisted repositories can run their initial checkout later, even
   after their checkout directory is removed, while failed unpersisted checkouts
   roll back their owned data.

### Bug Fixes

 - create SHA-256 repositories for `object_hash: None` in SHA-256-only builds
   Previously a SHA-1 repository was created that the same build couldn't open.
   Now `None` falls back to the build's default object format.
 - respect section trust for filesystem path protections
   <!-- agent -->
   GHSA-q54r-jf2p-rfr2 reports that path-protection configuration did not
   respect the section filter used for security-relevant settings. Use the
   filter for `core.protectHFS`, `core.protectNTFS`, and
   `gitoxide.core.protectWindows`, including the latter's early read for the
   reference store. Keep platform defaults and boolean error handling intact.
   
   Read-only fixtures exercise local and worktree configuration, full and
   reduced trust, custom filters, trusted API overrides, and malformed
   values in strict and lenient mode. Before the fix, reduced-trust settings
   replaced the defaults and a rejected malformed Windows setting prevented
   opening. Validation also exercises representative path names.
   
   Git baseline: the local Git reference identifies itself as `v2.56.GIT`.
   Its `t/t1014-read-tree-confusing.sh` and `read-cache.c:verify_path_internal`
   cover filesystem-specific path protections. Git's ownership policy in
   `setup.c:ensure_valid_ownership` rejects dubious ownership, whereas `gix`
   supports reduced trust by filtering configuration.
 - match Git clone reference handling and preserve offline defaults
   <!-- agent -->
   The prior CI run failed `check-mode` because `make_clone_refs.sh` had a
   shebang without its executable bit. Its ARM32 tests also ran Git 2.47.3,
   which rejects `clone --revision`; the matrix mistook that unsupported
   option for a clone failure and disagreed with successful `gix` clones.
   
   Mark the fixture executable and detect revision support from `git clone -h`.
   Skip only revision baselines on older Git, retaining all 72 other cases
   and the independent `gix` revision tests. Modern Git still exercises all
   81 baseline cases. Capture help despite its expected nonzero exit status.
 - match Git clone reference handling and preserve offline defaults
   <!-- agent -->
   `gix` clones recorded remote `HEAD` as a direct object ID, losing the
   branch relationship needed by later fetches and `Remote::default_branch()`.
   Bare clones also used the ordinary remote-tracking layout, while detached
   remote heads and custom destinations selected different references from
   `git clone`.
   
   Match Git's clone orchestration and reference selection:
   
   - Store bare-clone branches in `refs/heads/*`, without a default persisted
     fetch refspec, tracking `HEAD`, or branch upstream configuration. Keep
     explicit refspecs persistent and use `WithWorktree` plus `fetch_only()`
     for ordinary clones without a checkout.
   - Select the advertised symbolic target or guess a branch matching a
     detached `HEAD`, preferring `init.defaultBranch`, then `master`, then the
     first matching branch by name. Record the selected branch's first mapped
     peer before updating local `HEAD`, including overwriting a branch named
     `HEAD`; omit tracking `HEAD` when the selected target is excluded.
   - Detach and peel tag and revision selections, check out the selected
     `HEAD`, and align shallow selection, tag policy, initial packed-reference
     reflogs, and persisted revision configuration with Git. Preserve the
     reference directory required for repository discovery.
   
   Preserve fetch-source identity when deriving an offline default branch.
   Recognize `refs/heads/` sources and exact `heads/<name>` sources, including
   an exact source whose mapping was deduplicated against a glob. Return
   `None` for sources whose branch cannot be identified offline, count all
   ambiguous mappings, and share reverse mapping with upstream-branch lookup.
   
   Consult Git's `builtin/clone.c` and `remote.c`, and add deterministic
   Git-produced baselines for 27 cases in normal, no-checkout, and bare modes.
   Compare complete references, relevant configuration, reflog IDs, checkout
   contents, shallow boundaries, and success or failure with installed Git.
   Keep source fixtures read-only and read their existing refs through `gix`.
   Update API docs, CLI help and update printing, and affected clone/fetch tests.
   
   Known difference: replacing a direct branch named `HEAD` with the tracking
   symref logs a null old object ID in `gix-ref`; Git logs the resolved target.
   The baseline test explicitly checks this exception. Replacement-only custom
   refspecs remain a `gix` extension rather than being compared with Git's
   supplementary clone mappings.
 - resolve linked worktree submodules in their private Git directory
   <!-- agent -->
   Git stores each linked superproject's submodule repositories under
   `.git/worktrees/<id>/modules/<name>`, separately from the main worktree's
   `.git/modules/<name>` repositories. Using `common_dir()` for
   `Submodule::git_dir()` could open the main worktree's submodule before
   initialization or after deinitialization of the linked submodule.
   
   Derive the path from the superproject's `git_dir()` instead. Preserve name
   validation and the precedence of an existing submodule `.git` file.
   
   Cover initial checkout, initialization, and deinitialization using Git to
   populate a disposable linked worktree created by `gix`. Check that the main
   submodule remains populated and that linked repository state and opening
   follow its own lifecycle.
 - honor replacement refs and bypass stale commit graphs
   <!-- agent -->
   Enable standard replacement refs by default and honor `core.useReplaceRefs`
   with the same polarity as Git. The presence of `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS`
   disables them regardless of its value.
   
   Commit graphs contain original parent links, so skip them while object
   replacements are active, including when a caller forces or supplies a
   cache. Per-handle raw reads can still use the graph. Document the corrected
   opening and graph behavior.
   
   The regression first failed on the original code, then passed for ordinary
   open/discovery in bare and non-bare repositories, reopening after a graft,
   configuration and environment disablement, explicit raw reads, supplied
   and forced graphs, merge-base, and graph removal. All 503 `gix` integration
   tests passed; the regression also passed with only `revision,sha1` enabled.
   Native rebuilt `gix log` and `tix show` match Git across two grafts in both
   repository kinds with pre-existing raw graphs.

### Commit Statistics

 - 36 commits contributed to the release over the course of 14 calendar days.
 - 14 days passed between releases.
 - 16 commits were understood as [conventional](https://www.conventionalcommits.org).
 - 0 issues like '(#ID)' were seen in commit messages
